This document is the ground truth for a small internal service that lets staff submit travel and expense reports and lets managers approve them. It holds the context, the requirements, the architecture, two governance rules, a development standard, a business analyst note, the interfaces and the risks. Every work item specification cites it by section number.

## 1. Context and goals

### 1.1 Problem

Staff of a fictional retail company submit travel and expense reports by email and spreadsheet. A report waits 11 days on average for approval. Finance staff re-key every line into the ledger. Nobody can show who approved what, or when. Two audit findings last year named the missing trail.

### 1.2 Goals

| Id | Goal |
| --- | --- |
| G1 | A staff member submits a report with receipts from a web form. |
| G2 | The service sends each report to the right approvers without manual routing. |
| G3 | The service enforces approval limits and separation of duties (GOV-1). |
| G4 | Every state change is recorded in a trail that cannot be edited (GOV-2). |
| G5 | Approved reports reach the ledger by a nightly file, with no re-keying. |

### 1.3 Users and roles

| Role | What they do |
| --- | --- |
| Submitter | Creates and submits reports. Any employee. |
| Approver | Decides reports routed to them. Line managers and department heads. |
| Delegate | Decides on behalf of an approver for a set of dates. |
| Finance reviewer | Decides high value reports as the last step. Reads the export. |
| Auditor | Reads reports and the audit trail. Cannot change anything. |

### 1.4 Scope boundary

In scope: draft, submit, route, decide, notify, audit, export. Out of scope: paying the employee (the finance system does that), importing card feeds, mileage calculation, and currency conversion beyond the fixed rate table in section 3.3. Pilot recruitment and finance sign-off are owned by the program, not by the development plan.

## 2. Requirements

### 2.1 Functional requirements

| Id | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| FR-1 | A submitter creates a draft report with line items. Each line has a date, category, amount, currency, merchant and note. |
| FR-2 | A submitter attaches receipts to a report. Allowed types are PDF, PNG and JPEG. Each file is at most 10 MB. A report holds at most 20 receipts. |
| FR-3 | A submitter submits a draft. A submitted report cannot be edited, only returned by an approver. |
| FR-4 | The service routes a submitted report to approvers by the rules in section 3.5. |
| FR-5 | An approver sees an inbox of the reports waiting for their decision, oldest first. |
| FR-6 | An approver approves, rejects or returns a report, and must give a comment when rejecting or returning. |
| FR-7 | The submitter is notified of each decision and each state change. |
| FR-8 | An approver names a delegate for a range of dates. The delegate sees the approver's inbox for that range. |
| FR-9 | Approved reports are exported to the ledger every night in the file format of section 7.3. |
| FR-10 | An auditor reads the full trail of any report. |

### 2.2 Quality requirements

| Id | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| NFR-1 | The 95th percentile response time of the API is under 400 ms at 200 requests per second. |
| NFR-2 | Availability is 99.5 percent measured monthly, excluding planned maintenance. |
| NFR-3 | The web client meets WCAG 2.2 level AA. WCAG is the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines. |
| NFR-4 | Data stays in the company's home region. |
| NFR-5 | The recovery point objective is 15 minutes and the recovery time objective is 4 hours. |

## 3. Architecture

### 3.1 Overview

One service with one database, a receipt store, a message queue for notifications and a nightly export job.

```text
Web client --> API gateway --> Expense API --> PostgreSQL
                                   |  \--> Receipt store (object storage)
                                   |
                                   +--> Queue --> Notification worker --> Email
                                   |
                       Export job (02:00 UTC) --> Ledger drop folder
```

### 3.2 Components

| Component | Owner track | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web client | Experience | Report form, receipt upload, approver inbox, delegate screen. |
| Expense API | Workflow | REST API of section 7.1. Validates, stores, routes, decides. |
| Routing engine | Workflow | Builds the ordered list of approval steps for a report (section 3.5). |
| Rules module | Workflow | Applies the limits and separation of duties of GOV-1 on every decision. |
| Audit writer | Workflow | Appends events to the audit table (GOV-2). |
| Notification worker | Experience | Reads queue events and sends the emails of section 7.2. |
| Export job | Workflow | Writes the nightly ledger file (section 7.3). |
| Receipt store | Workflow | Holds receipt files. Keys are random and never derived from names. |

### 3.3 Data model

All identifiers are UUIDs. All timestamps are UTC. Amounts are integers in minor units (cents). A fixed rate table, maintained by finance and loaded as data, converts a line item currency to the base currency (USD).

| Table | Key fields |
| --- | --- |
| report | id, submitter_id, state, base_total_cents, submitted_at, decided_at, version |
| line_item | id, report_id, spent_on, category, amount_cents, currency, base_amount_cents, merchant, note |
| receipt | id, report_id, line_item_id (optional), object_key, content_type, size_bytes, sha256 |
| approval_step | id, report_id, position, role, approver_id, state, decided_at, comment |
| delegate | id, approver_id, delegate_id, starts_on, ends_on |
| audit_event | id, occurred_at, actor_id, report_id, event_type, from_state, to_state, detail (JSON) |

### 3.4 Report lifecycle

| From | Event | To | Who may cause it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Draft | submit | Submitted | Submitter |
| Submitted | routed | In approval | Service |
| In approval | approve (last step) | Approved | Approver or delegate |
| In approval | approve (not last step) | In approval | Approver or delegate |
| In approval | reject | Rejected | Approver or delegate |
| In approval | return | Returned | Approver or delegate |
| Returned | submit | Submitted | Submitter |
| Approved | export | Exported | Export job |

Rejected and Exported are final. Any other transition is refused with the error code E_STATE.

### 3.5 Routing

The routing engine builds the steps when a report moves from Submitted to In approval. It uses the base total of the report.

| Base total (USD) | Steps in order |
| --- | --- |
| Up to 500.00 | Line manager |
| 500.01 to 5,000.00 | Line manager, department head |
| 5,000.01 to 25,000.00 | Line manager, department head, finance reviewer |
| Above 25,000.00 | Not routed. The service returns E_LIMIT and the submitter follows the offline exception process. |

Rules that apply to every route.

1. If an approver in a step is the submitter, that step moves to the next person up the reporting line.
2. Steps are decided in order. A later step does not see the report until the earlier step approves.
3. A reminder goes to the current approver after 3 business days without a decision. After 5 business days the step escalates to the next person up the reporting line, and the audit trail records the escalation.
4. The routing result is stored as approval_step rows and does not change after routing, except by escalation.

### 3.6 Deployment

The service runs as one container behind the company gateway, in three environments: test, staging and production. Database migrations only move forward. The export job runs at 02:00 UTC and writes to the ledger drop folder. The whole feature sits behind the flag EXPENSE_APPROVALS_ENABLED (section 5.1). With the flag off the service starts, answers its health check and refuses every other request with the status 404.

## 4. Governance rules

### 4.1 GOV-1 Approval limits and separation of duties

Owner: the finance policy team. Applies to every decision, in every environment.

1. Nobody approves, rejects or returns their own report, directly or as a delegate.
2. An approver must stand above the submitter in the reporting line, or be a finance reviewer.
3. The people in the steps of one report must all be different people.
4. A delegate may act only for dates inside the delegate record, and never on a report that the delegator submitted.
5. Limits per step. A line manager's approval counts only for a base total up to 5,000.00. A department head's approval counts up to 25,000.00. Nothing above 25,000.00 can be approved in the service (section 3.5).
6. A refused decision returns the error code E_FORBIDDEN, names the rule number (for example GOV-1.3) and changes nothing.
7. The rules module applies these checks on the server for every decision. The web client may hide a button, but it is never the control.

### 4.2 GOV-2 Audit and retention

Owner: internal audit. Applies to every table named below.

1. Every state change of a report writes one audit_event in the same database transaction. If the audit write fails, the change fails.
2. The audit table is append only. The application account has insert and select rights on it and no update or delete right.
3. An audit_event records who, when, what changed (from_state and to_state), and a small detail object. It holds identifiers, never names, receipt contents or email addresses.
4. Reports, line items, approval steps and audit events are kept for 7 years from the decision date. Receipt files are kept as long as their report.
5. Deletion happens only by a retention job after the 7 years, and never for a report under a legal hold.
6. Log lines carry report identifiers and event types. They never carry amounts, comments or receipt contents.
7. Reading the audit trail of a report is itself recorded as an audit_event of type audit.viewed.

## 5. Development standard

### 5.1 DS-1 Delivery standard

Owner: the platform engineering team. Applies to every pull request.

1. Feature flag. All new behaviour sits behind EXPENSE_APPROVALS_ENABLED, off by default. With the flag off, nothing observable changes except the health check.
2. Tests. `npm test` runs the unit tests. `npm run test:contract` runs the contract tests against `contracts/openapi.yaml`. Both pass before a pull request merges.
3. Lint. `npm run lint` passes with no warnings.
4. Contracts first. `contracts/openapi.yaml` is the interface between the Workflow track and the Experience track. A change to it is its own pull request, announced at the next checkpoint.
5. Migrations. `npm run migrate` applies migrations. They only move forward. Each has a test that runs it on an empty database and on a copy of the previous schema.
6. Errors. Every error response uses the envelope of section 7.1.
7. Pull requests stay under 400 changed lines where possible. The description lists the acceptance criteria and the proof for each.
8. Commit messages are in the imperative mood. Secrets and personal data never appear in code, tests, logs or fixtures.

## 6. Business analyst note

Notes from eight interviews with submitters, managers and finance staff. They explain why the requirements read as they do.

### 6.1 What people asked for

| Id | Finding |
| --- | --- |
| BA-1 | Submitters want to start a report on a phone and finish it on a laptop. Drafts must be saved without a submit. |
| BA-2 | Managers decide in the gaps of their day. They want one inbox, the oldest report first, with the total and the submitter visible without opening it. |
| BA-3 | Finance wants one line in the ledger file per approved line item, with the cost centre, so nobody splits totals by hand. |
| BA-4 | Managers on leave leave reports waiting. A delegate for a date range fixes most of it. |
| BA-5 | Submitters want to know why a report was returned. A comment is not optional on a return. |
| BA-6 | Finance wants reminders early. Two business days is their preference. |

### 6.2 Edge cases the interviews surfaced

1. A single receipt can cover several line items, such as one hotel bill. The receipt belongs to the report, and the link to a line item is optional.
2. A report mixes currencies. Each line converts with the rate table. The report total is the sum of the converted lines, rounded half up to the cent after summing.
3. A returned report keeps its line items and receipts. The submitter edits and submits again, and the version number goes up.
4. A report submitted on a weekend counts its business days from the next Monday.
5. A manager who is also the submitter's friend is not a reason to skip a rule. Section 4.1 has no exceptions.
6. Finance asked for a reminder after 2 business days (BA-6). Section 3.5 says 3. The architecture document is the ground truth, so work items use 3. The next version of this document should settle the number.

## 7. Interfaces

### 7.1 REST API

All paths start with `/v1`. All bodies are JSON. The caller's identity comes from the gateway header `X-Employee-Id`, which the gateway sets and clients cannot forge.

| Method and path | Purpose | Success |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST /reports | Create a draft report. | 201 with the report |
| GET /reports/{id} | Read a report with line items, receipts and steps. | 200 |
| PUT /reports/{id} | Replace the line items of a draft or returned report. | 200 |
| POST /reports/{id}/receipts | Upload a receipt (multipart form). | 201 with the receipt |
| POST /reports/{id}/submit | Submit a draft or returned report. | 202 with the state |
| GET /inbox | List the reports waiting for the caller, oldest first. | 200 with a page |
| POST /reports/{id}/decisions | Approve, reject or return. | 200 with the report |
| PUT /delegates | Create or replace the caller's delegate record. | 200 |
| GET /reports/{id}/audit | Read the audit trail (auditors only). | 200 with a page |

Decision request.

```json
{ "decision": "approve", "comment": "" }
```

`decision` is `approve`, `reject` or `return`. `comment` is required and not blank for `reject` and `return`.

Error envelope used by every endpoint.

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "E_FORBIDDEN",
    "message": "GOV-1.3 refused this decision: the approver already decided an earlier step.",
    "rule": "GOV-1.3",
    "request_id": "9f0c1c0e-6a52-4c0f-b3a6-6d3a1a2c9a10"
  }
}
```

| Code | Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| E_VALIDATION | 400 | The body or a field fails its rule. The message names the field. |
| E_FORBIDDEN | 403 | A governance rule or a role check refused the call. `rule` names the rule. |
| E_NOT_FOUND | 404 | The report does not exist or the caller may not know it exists. |
| E_STATE | 409 | The transition is not allowed from the current state (section 3.4). |
| E_LIMIT | 422 | The base total is above 25,000.00 and cannot be routed. |

### 7.2 Notification event

The API puts one event on the queue for each state change. The worker turns it into an email.

```json
{
  "event_id": "string, UUID",
  "event_type": "report.state_changed",
  "occurred_at": "string, UTC timestamp",
  "report_id": "string, UUID",
  "from_state": "string, one of the states in 3.4",
  "to_state": "string, one of the states in 3.4",
  "recipient_id": "string, employee id",
  "comment_present": "boolean"
}
```

The event never carries amounts, comments or names. The worker reads those from the API with the service account when it builds the email.

### 7.3 Ledger export file

One file per night, named `expenses-YYYYMMDD.csv`, with a second file `expenses-YYYYMMDD.sha256` that holds the SHA-256 checksum of the first. One row per approved line item of every report that moved to Approved since the last export. After writing, the job moves those reports to Exported.

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| report_id | UUID of the report |
| line_item_id | UUID of the line item |
| employee_id | Submitter |
| cost_centre | Cost centre of the submitter at approval time |
| spent_on | Date of the expense, YYYY-MM-DD |
| category | Category code |
| amount_cents | Amount in the line currency, integer |
| currency | ISO 4217 currency code |
| base_amount_cents | Amount in USD, integer |
| approved_at | UTC timestamp of the last approval |

## 8. Risks and decisions

### 8.1 Risks

| Id | Risk | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | The reporting line data is out of date, so routing picks the wrong manager. | Routing reads the line once at submit time and records it. Finance can ask for a re-route. |
| R2 | Managers ignore reminders and reports pile up. | Escalation after 5 business days (section 3.5). The pilot measures time to decision. |
| R3 | The export format changes after finance review. | The file format sits in one module and a contract test. The program owns the sign-off. |
| R4 | Receipts hold personal data. | Receipt store keys are random. Receipts are never logged or put in events (GOV-2). |
| R5 | The two tracks drift on the API. | Contracts first (DS-1.4) and a joint check at every checkpoint. |

### 8.2 Decisions

| Id | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| D1 | One PostgreSQL database holds reports and the audit trail, so a state change and its audit event share a transaction. |
| D2 | The inbox is read by polling in version 1. Push comes later if the pilot asks for it. |
| D3 | Currency conversion uses a fixed rate table loaded as data, not a live feed. |
| D4 | The feature flag is a single process-wide setting in version 1. |
